Null bitdensity threshold: s(ll, k = 20) quantile regression + GPD tail (tau = 0.99)

What this document does, and the assumptions it makes

Given a Foldseek search of random (“null”) proteins against the target structure DB, this notebook builds an alignment-length-keyed background threshold for bitdensity = bits / (qend - qstart + 1), plus a GPD tail on its exceedances. The steps, in order:

  1. Reduce the null with a binomial identity test (Bonferroni, alpha = 0.05). A handful of “null” queries are actually detectable homologs. We flag them with a per-alignment binomial test on the number of identical residues and drop the significant ones, so the surviving set is a clean chance background.
  2. Fit the threshold bitdensity ~ s(ll, k = 20) (ll = log alignment length) by ALD (asymmetric-Laplace) quantile regression and check its exceedance calibration across alignment length.
  3. Sweep the quantile tau for that threshold and check GPD tail-parameter stability across threshold choices.
  4. At tau = 0.99, take the excesses and compare a constant vs. an s(ll)-varying GPD scale with the probability integral transform (PIT) QQ plot; the constant scale is adopted.
  5. Export the model to random_protein_null/exports_gam_bin_evt — a per-aln_len lookup of the threshold u and GPD sigma, the constant GPD tail parameters, and the null samples.

Assumptions introduced here (not part of the raw data):

  • Binomial identity model. Identical residues along an alignment are treated as i.i.d. Bernoulli(q(L)), so the identical-residue count is Binomial(aln_len, q(L)). This ignores positional correlation and is an approximation used only to flag obvious homologs.
  • Chance identity q(L). Estimated by a qgam median smooth ident ~ s(log aln_len) (the binned a + b / sqrt(L) curve and the Rost twilight-zone curve are drawn alongside for reference only, not used in the filter).
  • Threshold model. bitdensity ~ s(log aln_len, k = 20), ALD quantile regression with evgam, at tau = 0.99 for the operative export.
  • GPD tail. Excesses over the threshold follow a Generalised Pareto with a constant scale and constant shape (log link). An s(log aln_len)-varying scale is compared in step 4 and the constant scale is adopted on the PIT-exponential QQ evidence.
  • Extrapolation for the export lookup. For aln_len below the smallest observed value, the smooth is evaluated at the boundary (ll clamped to log(min observed aln_len)) and the row is flagged extrapolated = TRUE.
  • bitdensity is only defined where an alignment exists, so no-hit rows are dropped before any modelling.
# Original best-hits with a 70% target-coverage filter applied to every hit (min tcov = 0.70).
# (The `best_hits_random_model_no_cov.tsv` variant has no coverage filter.)

Query lengths from the FASTA

Length is read directly from random_null_candidates.fasta. Headers look like >ACCESSION length_bin=... organism="..."; parse_fasta_lengths() takes the first whitespace-delimited token as the id, so the extra description text is ignored.

parse_fasta_lengths <- function(path) {
  lines <- readLines(path)
  header_idx <- which(startsWith(lines, ">"))
  ids <- sub("^>(\\S+).*", "\\1", lines[header_idx])
  starts <- header_idx + 1L
  ends   <- c(header_idx[-1] - 1L, length(lines))
  seq_lengths <- mapply(function(s, e) if (s > e) 0L else sum(nchar(lines[s:e])), starts, ends)
  tibble(query = ids, length = as.integer(seq_lengths))
}

fasta_lengths <- parse_fasta_lengths(fasta_file)
fasta_lengths_toxprot <-parse_fasta_lengths(mature_toxprot)
n_dup <- sum(duplicated(fasta_lengths$query))
if (n_dup > 0) {

}

Build the score table

For every candidate in the FASTA, look up its bitscore in the null-model table. If the query has no row there (no alignment survived Foldseek’s own filtering), the alignment is treated as bitscore 0 and aln_len (= qend - qstart + 1) is set to 0 rather than dropping the query.

add_score_columns <- function(tbl) {
  tbl %>%
    left_join(null_model %>% select(query, target, qstart, qend, bits, evalue, pident,tend,tstart),
              by = "query") %>%
    mutate(
      in_null_table = !is.na(bits),
      bits          = ifelse(in_null_table, bits, 0),
      evalue        = pmax(evalue, 1e-75),
      aln_len       = ifelse(in_null_table, qend - qstart + 1, 0),
      bitdensity    = case_when(!in_null_table ~ 0,
                                aln_len > 0     ~ bits / aln_len,
                                TRUE            ~ NA_real_),
      ll = log(ifelse(in_null_table, qend - qstart + 1, 0)),  # log alignment length
      lm = log(length)  )                                # log full query length
    }

analysis_tbl <- fasta_lengths %>% add_score_columns()

cat("Candidate queries analysed:      ", nrow(analysis_tbl), "\n")

Step 1 — Reduce the null with a binomial identity test (Bonferroni, alpha = 0.05)

A few “null” queries are genuine homologs: they share more identical residues than chance allows. We estimate the length-dependent chance identity q(L), then for each alignment compute the probability of seeing at least n_ident = round(pident/100 * aln_len) identities under Binomial(aln_len, q(L)), Bonferroni-correct across all alignments, and drop alignments whose adjusted p-value is <= 0.05 (real homologs). The rest stay in the null.

hits <- hits %>% mutate(n_ident = round(pident / 100 * aln_len),
                      ll=log(aln_len),
                      ident_hundred=pident/100)

# Binned background identity, then q(L) = a + b / sqrt(L)
# --- add dispersion diagnostics to qtab --------------------------------
qtab <- hits %>%
  mutate(bin = cut(aln_len, c(0, 20, 40, 60, 80, 120, 160, 250, 500))) %>%
  group_by(bin) %>%
  summarise(n       = n(),
            L       = median(aln_len, na.rm = TRUE),
            q_med   = median(pident, na.rm = TRUE) / 100,
            q_mle   = sum(n_ident, na.rm = TRUE) / sum(aln_len, na.rm = TRUE),
            sd_emp  = sd(ident_hundred, na.rm = TRUE),
            mad_raw = mad(ident_hundred, constant = 1, na.rm = TRUE),  # unscaled
            mad_sc  = mad(ident_hundred, na.rm = TRUE),                # 1.4826 (R default)
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(sd_binom  = sqrt(q_med * (1 - q_med) / L),
         ratio_sd  = sd_emp / sd_binom,
         ratio_mad = mad_sc / sd_binom,
         lab       = sprintf("MAD %.3f (%.2f\u00d7)\nSD %.3f (%.2f\u00d7)",
                             mad_sc, ratio_mad, sd_emp, ratio_sd))

qfit    <- nls(q_med ~ a + b / sqrt(L), data = qtab, start = list(a = 0.09, b = 0.7))

# The qgam identity smooth is the slowest fit in the notebook; cache it to disk so re-runs
# load it instead of refitting. Delete cache/med_fit.rds (or the whole cache/ dir) to refresh.
cache_dir <- "C:/Masters_data/Master_thesis/foldseek_search/random_protein_null/cache"
dir.create(cache_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
med_cache <- file.path(cache_dir, "med_fit.rds")
if (file.exists(med_cache)) {
  med_fit <- readRDS(med_cache)
} else {
  med_fit <- qgam(ident_hundred ~ s(ll), data = hits, qu = 0.50)
  saveRDS(med_fit, med_cache)
}

disp_tab <- function(df, label) {
  df %>%
    mutate(bin = cut(aln_len, c(0, 20, 40, 60, 80, 120, 160, 250, 500))) %>%
    group_by(bin) %>%
    summarise(n = n(), L = median(aln_len), q_med = median(pident)/100,
              sd_emp = sd(ident_hundred), mad_sc = mad(ident_hundred),
              .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(sd_binom  = sqrt(q_med * (1 - q_med) / L),
           ratio_sd  = sd_emp  / sd_binom,
           ratio_mad = mad_sc  / sd_binom,
           eps_mom   = pmax(0, sd_emp^2 - sd_binom^2) / (0.234^2),  # refit delta per bin
           set = label)
}
q_global <- median(hits$pident, na.rm = TRUE) / 100

grid <- data.frame(aln_len = seq(4, 500, length.out = 600))
grid$q_fit <- predict(qfit, newdata = data.frame(L = grid$aln_len))
grid$q_qgam <- predict(med_fit, newdata = data.frame(ll = log(grid$aln_len)),type = "response")

# Rost twilight-zone curve, drawn for reference only (not used in the filter).
rost <- function(L) ifelse(L > 450, 19.5, 480 * L^(-0.32 * (1 + exp(-L / 1000)))) / 100

ggplot() +
  geom_line(data = grid, aes(aln_len, q_fit, colour = "fitted q(L) = a + b/sqrt(L)"),

hits <- hits %>%

The reduced null used from here on (rows with a finite bitdensity):

d <- null_kept %>% filter(is.finite(bitdensity), is.finite(ll))
cat("Modelling rows (reduced null): ", nrow(d), "\n")
## Modelling rows (reduced null):  63263

Step 2 — Quantile-regression threshold: bitdensity ~ s(ll, k = 20)

The threshold for bitdensity = bits / (qend - qstart + 1) is a smooth of log alignment length, fit by ALD quantile regression at tau = 0.99. The calibration plot shows the realised exceedance rate (fraction of null hits above the fitted threshold) in equal-count bins of log alignment length; a well-calibrated threshold sits flat on the target 1 - tau.

tau <- 0.99
fit_calib <- evgam(bitdensity ~ s(ll, k = 20), data = d,
                   family = "ald", ald.args = list(tau = tau))
d$u_calib <- as.numeric(predict(fit_calib, newdata = d)$location)
d$hit     <- as.numeric(d$bitdensity > d$u_calib)

calib <- d %>%
  mutate(g = cut(ll, unique(quantile(ll, seq(0, 1, length.out = 17))), include.lowest = TRUE)) %>%
  group_by(g) %>%
  summarise(v = mean(hit), n = n(), ll = mean(ll), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(n >= 25) %>%
  mutate(se = sqrt((1 - tau) * tau / n),
         lo = pmax((1 - tau) - 1.96 * se, 0), hi = (1 - tau) + 1.96 * se)

ggplot(calib, aes(ll, v)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), fill = "grey90") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1 - tau, linetype = 2, colour = "grey20") +
  geom_line(colour = "#0072B2", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(colour = "#0072B2", size = 1.5) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 0.05)) +
  labs(x = "log(alignment length)", y = "realised exceedance rate",
       title = "Calibration of bitdensity ~ s(ll, k = 20) at tau = 0.99",
       subtitle = paste0("Target ", 1 - tau, " (dashed); grey band = 95% binomial interval"),
       caption = sprintf("Reduced null, n = %s.", format(nrow(d), big.mark = ","))) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12)

Step 3 — Sweep tau for the s(ll, k = 20) threshold

Refit bitdensity ~ s(ll, k = 20) at several tau, fit a constant Generalised-Pareto tail to the excesses at each, and check that the GPD scale and shape are stable across threshold choices (a signature of a genuine GPD tail). The sweep (five ALD fits, each with a 200-sample GPD bootstrap) is cached to cache/tau_sweep_bitdensity_k20.rds; set force_recompute_sweep <- TRUE to refit.

taus <- c(0.90, 0.95, 0.975, 0.99, 0.995)
tau_sweep_cache       <- file.path(cache_dir, "tau_sweep_bitdensity_k20.rds")
force_recompute_sweep <- FALSE

fit_at_tau <- function(dat, tau) {
  fu <- evgam(bitdensity ~ s(ll, k = 20), data = dat,
              family = "ald", ald.args = list(tau = tau))
  dat$u     <- as.numeric(predict(fu, newdata = dat)$location)
  ex        <- subset(dat, bitdensity > u)
  ex$excess <- ex$bitdensity - ex$u
  list(fit_u = fu, exc = ex, u = dat$u)
}

gpd_pars <- function(ex) {
  g  <- evgam(list(excess ~ 1, ~ 1), data = ex, family = "gpd")
  pr <- predict(g, newdata = ex[1, , drop = FALSE], type = "response")
  c(scale = as.numeric(pr$scale[1]), shape = as.numeric(pr$shape[1]))
}

boot_pars <- function(ex, B = 200) {
  out <- t(replicate(B, {
    bs <- ex[sample(nrow(ex), replace = TRUE), ]
    tryCatch(gpd_pars(bs), error = function(e) c(scale = NA, shape = NA))
  }))
  out[complete.cases(out), , drop = FALSE]
}

if (!force_recompute_sweep && file.exists(tau_sweep_cache)) {
  res <- readRDS(tau_sweep_cache)
} else {
  set.seed(1)
  res <- lapply(taus, function(tt) {
    message("sweep tau = ", tt)
    f  <- fit_at_tau(d, tt)
    pt <- gpd_pars(f$exc)
    bt <- boot_pars(f$exc, B = 200)
    data.frame(
      tau      = tt,
      n_exc    = nrow(f$exc),
      scale    = pt["scale"], shape = pt["shape"],
      scale_lo = quantile(bt[, "scale"], 0.025), scale_hi = quantile(bt[, "scale"], 0.975),
      shape_lo = quantile(bt[, "shape"], 0.025), shape_hi = quantile(bt[, "shape"], 0.975),
      u_mean   = mean(f$u)
    )
  }) %>% bind_rows()
  saveRDS(res, tau_sweep_cache)
}

  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(scale, shape), names_to = "par", values_to = "est") %>%
  mutate(lo  = ifelse(par == "scale", scale_lo, shape_lo),
         hi  = ifelse(par == "scale", scale_hi, shape_hi),
         par = factor(par, c("scale", "shape"), c("sigma (scale)", "xi (shape)"))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(tau, est)) +
  geom_hline(data = data.frame(par = factor("xi (shape)", c("sigma (scale)", "xi (shape)"))),
             aes(yintercept = 0), linetype = 2, colour = "grey50") +

  geom_point(size = 2.2, colour = "#D55E00") +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0("n=", n_exc)), vjust = -1.4, size = 2.8, colour = "grey35") +
  facet_wrap(~ par, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = expression(tau), y = "estimate",
       title = "GPD parameter stability across threshold quantiles (s(ll, k = 20))",
       subtitle = "Constant GPD scale and shape; 95% bootstrap intervals (B = 200)") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11)

Step 4 — GPD estimation at the operative tau (s(ll, k = 20) threshold)

Fix the operative threshold quantile at tau = 0.99, fit bitdensity ~ s(ll, k = 20) there, take the excesses, and fit two GPD tails: a constant scale and a scale varying as s(ll) (both with constant shape). We judge them with the probability integral transform: under a correct GPD the transformed excess w = (1/xi) * log(1 + xi * exc / sigma) is standard exponential, so a QQ plot of w against Exp(1) quantiles should fall on the diagonal. The operative fit is cached to cache/operative_bitdensity_k20.rds.

tau_export         <- 0.99
op_cache           <- file.path(cache_dir, "operative_bitdensity_k20.rds")
force_recompute_op <- FALSE

if (!force_recompute_op && file.exists(op_cache)) {
  op <- readRDS(op_cache)
} else {
  fit_u <- evgam(bitdensity ~ s(ll, k = 20), data = d,
                 family = "ald", ald.args = list(tau = tau_export))
  d$u   <- as.numeric(predict(fit_u, newdata = d)$location)
  d$exc <- d$bitdensity - d$u
  ex    <- filter(d, exc > 0)
  op <- list(fit_u = fit_u, ex = ex, zeta = mean(d$exc > 0), n_total = nrow(d),
             tau_export = tau_export,
             fit_g_const = evgam(list(exc ~ 1,     ~ 1), data = ex, family = "gpd"),
             fit_g_var   = evgam(list(exc ~ s(ll), ~ 1), data = ex, family = "gpd"))
  saveRDS(op, op_cache)
}

fit_u       <- op$fit_u;        ex         <- op$ex
zeta        <- op$zeta;         tau_export <- op$tau_export
fit_g_const <- op$fit_g_const;  fit_g_var  <- op$fit_g_var

# u / exc on every null row for the threshold curve and the export below.
d$u   <- as.numeric(predict(fit_u, newdata = d)$location)
d$exc <- d$bitdensity - d$u
c(n_exc = nrow(ex), p_exceed = zeta)
##        n_exc     p_exceed 
## 662.00000000   0.01046425
# PIT of a GPD excess to a standard exponential.
to_exp <- function(y, s, x) ifelse(abs(x) < 1e-6, y / s, log1p(x * y / s) / x)
pit <- bind_rows(
  {p <- predict(fit_g_const, newdata = ex, type = "response")
   tibble(w = to_exp(ex$exc, p$scale, p$shape), model = "constant scale")},
  {p <- predict(fit_g_var, newdata = ex, type = "response")
   tibble(w = to_exp(ex$exc, p$scale, p$shape), model = "scale ~ s(log l)")}
)
pit_q <- pit %>%
  group_by(model) %>%
  arrange(w, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(i    = row_number(),
         nn   = n(),
         theo = qexp(i / (nn + 1)),
         lo   = qexp(qbeta(0.025, i, nn - i + 1)),
         hi   = qexp(qbeta(0.975, i, nn - i + 1))) %>%
  ungroup()

band <- pit_q %>% filter(model == first(model))   # same n in both -> one ribbon

ggplot(pit_q, aes(theo, w)) +
  geom_ribbon(data = band, aes(x = theo, ymin = lo, ymax = hi),
              inherit.aes = FALSE, fill = "grey85", alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = 2, colour = "grey40") +
  geom_point(aes(colour = model), size = 0.8, alpha = 0.6) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("constant scale"   = "grey50",
                                 "scale ~ s(log l)" = "#D55E00"), name = NULL) +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(x = "theoretical Exp(1) quantile", y = "PIT-transformed excess",
       title = "PIT-exponential QQ plot: constant vs ll-varying GPD scale",
       subtitle = paste0("s(ll, k = 20) threshold, tau = ", tau_export, ", n = ", nrow(ex),
                         "; grey band = 95% pointwise interval under Exp(1)")) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

Both scales lie inside the 95% band, so they are hard to separate statistically (the two shapes agree to within ~1 SE). Given that, we adopt the simpler constant-scale GPD with constant shape. The histogram below overlays that fitted GPD density on the exceedances — it tracks them closely. Note only the tail scale is constant here; the threshold u(ll) itself stays length-dependent.

# Constant-scale GPD: a single sigma and a single shape.
gp    <- predict(fit_g_const, newdata = ex[1, , drop = FALSE], type = "response")
sig_c <- as.numeric(gp$scale[1])
xi_c  <- as.numeric(gp$shape[1])

dgpd <- function(y, sigma, xi){
  if (abs(xi) < 1e-8)
    {dexp(y, rate = 1 / sigma)}
  else
    {ifelse(1 + xi * y / sigma > 0, (1 / sigma) * (1 + xi * y / sigma)^(-1 / xi - 1), 0)}
}
dens <- data.frame(exc = seq(0, max(ex$exc), length.out = 400))
dens$d <- dgpd(dens$exc, sig_c, xi_c)

ggplot(ex, aes(exc)) +
  geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(density)), bins = 40,
                 fill = "#2c7fb8", colour = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_line(data = dens, aes(exc, d), colour = "#D55E00", linewidth = 1.1) +
  labs(x = "excess over threshold  (bitdensity - u)", y = "density",
       title = "Exceedances with the constant-scale GPD overlaid",
       subtitle = sprintf("tau = %.3f, n = %d   |   sigma = %.3f, shape xi = %.3f",
                          tau_export, nrow(ex), sig_c, xi_c)) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

The fitted threshold u(aln_len) across alignment length:

aln_min <- min(d$aln_len); aln_max <- max(d$aln_len)

curve <- data.frame(aln_len = seq(aln_min, aln_max, length.out = 800))
curve$ll <- log(curve$aln_len)
curve$u  <- as.numeric(predict(fit_u, newdata = curve)$location)

ggplot() +
  geom_point(data = d, aes(aln_len, bitdensity), size = 0.3, alpha = 0.15) +
  geom_line(data = curve, aes(aln_len, u), colour = "#a00101", linewidth = 1.1) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 7.5)) +
  labs(x = "alignment length (aa)", y = expression(u[0.99] ~ "  [bitdensity]"),
       title = expression(paste("Null bitdensity threshold ", U(aln_len), ": ", tau, " = 0.99"))) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 15)

Step 5 — Export the model to exports_gam_bin_evt

Writes four files to random_protein_null/exports_gam_bin_evt (the other files already in that directory are left untouched):

  • u99_sigma_alnlen_lookup.csv — per-aln_len threshold u (length-dependent) and GPD sigma (a single constant, repeated per row), with an extrapolated flag (TRUE below the smallest observed aln_len, where ll is clamped to the boundary).
  • gpd_tail_params.csv — the constant GPD scale and shape (with the shape’s standard error), p_exceed, the counts, and the aln_len range.
  • null_bitdensity_sample.csv — the reduced-null sample (aln_len, length, bitdensity).
  • null_excess_sample.csv — the positive exceedances (exc).
export_dir <- "C:/Masters_data/Master_thesis/random_protein_null/exports_gam_bin_evt"
dir.create(export_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

# --- constant-scale GPD: single shape (+ SE) and a single scale ----------------
shape_tab <- summary(fit_g_const)[[1]]$shape          # parametric-terms table for the shape
shape_hat <- shape_tab[1, "Estimate"]
se_shape  <- shape_tab[1, "Std. Error"]
scale_hat <- as.numeric(predict(fit_g_const, newdata = ex[1, , drop = FALSE],
                                type = "response")$scale[1])   # sigma is constant

# --- per-aln_len lookup; clamp ll at the boundary for aln_len below the minimum -
# u varies with alignment length; sigma is the single constant tail scale.
lut <- tibble(aln_len = seq_len(aln_max)) %>%
  mutate(ll = log(pmax(aln_len, aln_min)))
lut$u     <- as.numeric(predict(fit_u, newdata = lut)$location)   # evgam ALD -> $location
lut$sigma <- scale_hat                                            # constant
lut <- lut %>%
  mutate(extrapolated = aln_len < aln_min) %>%
  select(aln_len, u, sigma, extrapolated)

# --- tail parameter summary ---------------------------------------------------
gpd_tail_params <- tibble(
  threshold_tau = tau_export,
  p_exceed      = zeta,
  shape         = shape_hat,
  se_shape      = se_shape,
  scale         = scale_hat,          # single constant sigma (also filled per-row in the lookup)
  n_exceedances = nrow(ex),
  n_total       = op$n_total,
  aln_len_min   = aln_min,
  aln_len_max   = aln_max,
  u_formula     = "s(log(aln_len), k = 20), evgam ALD quantile regression (tau = 0.99)",
  sigma_formula = "constant (exc ~ 1), log link"
)

readr::write_csv(d %>% select(aln_len, length, bitdensity),
                 file.path(export_dir, "null_bitdensity_sample.csv"))
readr::write_csv(ex %>% select(exc),
                 file.path(export_dir, "null_excess_sample.csv"))
readr::write_csv(lut,
                 file.path(export_dir, "u99_sigma_alnlen_lookup.csv"))
readr::write_csv(gpd_tail_params,
                 file.path(export_dir, "gpd_tail_params.csv"))
